bib.title: Evaluating Skills, Not Just Agents: Agentic Continuous Evaluation of Skills

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Evaluating Skills, Not Just Agents: Agentic Continuous Evaluation of Skills" (ACES). Christopher Kevin (corresponding, christopherk@nvidia.com), Narendran Raghavan, Jean-Francois Puget, Roshni Malani, Meghana Puvvadi, Moshe Abramovitch, Mohit Gupta, Rama Akkiraju, Subodh Prabhu, Yogesh Dangi, Wei Luo, Seong Hee Lee. All NVIDIA. arXiv:2608.20614v1 [cs.AI], 20 Aug 2026. Preprint with ACM-style CCS tags, no venue stated. Code: NVIDIA SkillEvaluator (open source, Tier 3 = ACES).

COVERAGE: All 15 pages, 85,527 of 85,527 chars read. References (about 70,000 onward) skimmed only. Appendices A to D read. Figures were read from their captions only, not as images. I also read note 06 lines 1-356 and grepped the rest.

CORE CLAIM: Scan-only skill gates (structural checks, LLM-judge rubrics, linters, security scans) never run the skill and do not predict whether it helps a live agent. ACES measures a skill (a SKILL.md package) by running paired with-skill and without-skill trials, with other "decoy" skills held fixed in both arms. It reports Skill Lift, the with-skill minus baseline score under a fixed agent, model, task, workspace and grader.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Mean composite Skill Lift is +0.2134 over 947 paired cases.
  number: 0.2134, 95% CI [0.1967, 0.2301]; absolute means 0.7460 with skill vs 0.5326 baseline
  setup: 58 of 64 production skills, 4 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Terminus-2), 177 scored skill-agent cells. Composite is the equal-weight (1/6) mean of 6 metrics. Graders are deterministic checks plus LLM/RAGAS judges. Judge models for live grading are not named.
  quote: "the mean paired composite Skill Lift is 0.2134 with a 95% normal CI of [0.1967, 0.2301], from absolute condition means of 0.7460 with skill and 0.5326 at baseline."
  where: §6.4, p10
- Outcome-only lift is smaller than the composite: 0.1799. Accuracy +0.1431 (0.7760 vs 0.6329), goal accuracy +0.2167 (0.6887 vs 0.4720). Process metrics gain most.
  number: skill_execution +0.3263, behavior_check +0.2983, skill_efficiency +0.2758, security +0.020 (Fig 8)
  quote: "the skill-execution metric improves by 0.3263, behavior checking by 0.2983, and skill efficiency by 0.2758."
  where: §6.4 and Appendix A
  Caveat: skill_execution and behavior_check check things the baseline "may be unable to satisfy when the target skill is withheld" (their words, App. A), so part of the process lift is built in by design.
- Lift is mostly positive but not always.
  number: 689 positive, 171 zero, 87 negative cases; median 0.1717. Skill efficiency was positive in only 41.7% of cases.
  quote: "Composite lift is positive in 689 cases, zero in 171, and negative in 87 (median 0.1717)"
  where: §6.4
  In the 201-cell aggregate, 11 cells have negative mean lift and 11 have zero (§6.6).
- Static scores do not predict live lift.
  number: Tier 1 structural rho = -0.0181 (95% CI [-0.2667, 0.2327]); Tier 2 LLM-judge rho = -0.0266 (CI [-0.2745, 0.2247])
  setup: n = 62 skills with both scan and live data
  quote: "These correlations are statistically indistinguishable from zero."
  where: §6.7, p11
- The two scan methods barely agree.
  number: Spearman 0.14 (Pearson 0.08); 94.5% pass the structural gate at 70, 48.9% reach 80, 86.2% pass the judge at 70
  setup: n = 145 skills, mixed internal and public. Structural score is about 50 rules in 4 weighted dimensions. Judge is G-Eval style, temperature 0, 9+1 criteria. Judge spread across Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku and a 9B in-house model is about 1.5 points on 0-10.
  quote: "the deterministic structural score and the LLM-judge overall score correlate at Spearman ρ= 0.14 (Pearson r= 0.08; Figure 1, right)."
  where: §2.4, p4
- Stronger models shrink lift because the baseline rises.
  number: Codex harness, GPT-5.2/5.4/5.5: baseline 0.63/0.67/0.71, with-skill 0.73/0.77/0.76, lift +0.09/+0.11/+0.05 (Fig 10c)
  setup: the paper calls it "a methodological demonstration, not a broad model-quality claim"
  quote: "absolute scores can rise while marginal skill lift shrinks as the baseline model improves"
  where: Abstract, §6.5, §7
- Lift varies a lot by harness.
  number: OpenCode 0.3611, Claude Code 0.2904, Codex 0.1264, Terminus-2 0.0896
  setup: matched deltas against each harness's own baseline, with uneven coverage (Claude Code 56 cells/251 cases, Codex 50/259, OpenCode 34/211, Terminus-2 37/226). Not a model ranking.
  where: §6.5
- Routing stress test: lift holds as the number of visible skills grows, until 50.
  number: lift 0.133-0.149 for 1-20 visible skills; wall time 258 s at 1 skill to 451 s at 20; at 50 skills with-skill pass rate 0.55 (0.725 at 1) and 1,290 s
  setup: 25 variants, 5 target skills, 1/5/10/20/50 visible skills, 2 harnesses
  where: §6.5 and App. B
- Method point: use a baseline that keeps decoy skills, and split lift into isolation and group modes. Lift_grp minus Lift_iso is the "routing premium".
  number: none
  quote: "The naive baseline thus inflates lift by attributing both to the skill."
  where: §4.7-4.8
- Missingness sensitivity: if every baseline-scored but with-skill-unscored case is imputed as a with-skill failure, composite lift falls from 0.2153 to 0.1840 but stays positive.
  setup: raw-row audit that reconstructed 898 of 947 pairs
  where: App. B
- Cost scaling: up to 2NKCA container runs for N skills, K agents, C cases, A attempts, 2 conditions.
  quote: "𝑁 skills×𝐾 agents×𝐶 cases×𝐴 attempts× 2conditions requires up to2𝑁𝐾𝐶𝐴 container runs"
  where: §4.6

LIMITS
Stated by the authors:
- Live inter-judge agreement, human calibration and judge-uncertainty propagation are "unmeasured". The 1.5-point judge spread covers document rubrics only.
- Lift is a marginal contribution under the declared workspace and baseline, not an intrinsic skill value.
- Repeated runs are partial: 88 of 201 cells have 2 trials, 113 have 1. For the 88 repeated cells the median within-cell SD is 0.0319 and the mean 0.0699.
- The corpus skews to System Access, Deployment, Platform and Data Infra.
- Some skills need a VPN the container cannot cross, so goal accuracy is a lower bound there.
- Timeouts are lumped with other no-score causes.
- No formal tests for negative-lift classes.
- Raw trajectories are not released.
- The headline CI treats cases as independent. Cluster bootstraps give [0.1898, 0.2350] over skills and [0.1880, 0.2385] over cells.
- The equal 1/6 weights are "an inspectable diagnostic default, not a claim that the metrics are equally causal".

Unstated or my reading:
- No named models for the production runs (only the Codex slice names GPT-5.x, and Fig 10b names Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.2-Codex). The grader model for live metrics is not given.
- Authors are NVIDIA and the corpus is mostly internal, so there is a possible selection and self-evaluation bias.
- Evals are author-written, so tasks may favour the skill. expected_behavior items are written around the skill's workflow.
- The OpenClaw security case is n=1 and excluded from the aggregate.
- No ablation of equal weighting, no baseline-model-fixed comparison of the process metrics, and no human check of any live judge.
- The paper's "dated" risk: judge models named (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, 3.5 Haiku) are old.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES (minor)
- The Lift definition says M "contains" 4 metrics, then "also includes" the other 2. The abstract says 6.
- 578 "condition runs" in Table 6 against 947 paired cases (which need at least 1,894 condition scores). This is unexplained, and likely a different unit.
- Fig 10c deltas (0.09/0.11/0.05) differ from the Codex rows in Fig 10a (0.13) and 10b (0.11). These are different cell sets, but it is not explained. 0.73-0.63 is shown as 0.09.
- The raw-row audit gives 0.2153 composite, 0.2180 goal accuracy and 0.1805 outcome, against the frozen 0.2134, 0.2167 and 0.1799. Small, and explained as a subset (898 vs 947).
- The related-work section says SkillsBench has "a fixed 84-task set". Note 06 says 87 tasks. Check against the SkillsBench source.
- Stress-test lift of about 0.14 at 1 visible skill differs from the 0.2134 headline. It uses a different skill set (5 targets).
- Arithmetic otherwise checks: six lifts average to 0.2133, harness means weight to 0.2133, 251+259+211+226=947.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- G-Eval (refs 12, 23) for the judge pattern.
- RAGAS (ref 13) AgentGoalAccuracyWithReference.
- Harbor and ATIF (refs 17, 18).
- SkillsBench (11, 32), "Skills in the Wild" (22), SkillTester (35), AEVAL (Anand et al. 2026, arXiv:2607.16345), SWE-CI (Chen et al. 2026, arXiv:2603.03823).
- Anthropic "Demystifying Evals for AI Agents" (2026) and the Anthropic skills docs.
- OpenAI Codex team's prompting taxonomy for the four-bucket dataset: explicit, implicit, contextual, negative control.
- Process-evaluation work (ref 15).
- Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, AgentBench, MCP-Bench (arXiv:2508.20453) and MCPEval.

TARGET NOTE FIT
- Best-fit section: "Scoring tool calls", in the paragraph at line 186 ("Do the same for anything you add to an agent. SkillsBench ran 87 tasks with and without curated Skills..."). ACES is the same with/without-component design, applied to author-owned tasks with decoy skills held fixed.
- Already covered in the note: the SkillsBench with/without lift (line 186), the no-baseline-tool paragraph (line 184), harness-matters (Terminal-Bench, Harness-IF, AutoLab), router/skill component evals (line 197 on), and the Albada recall/precision metrics.
- Missing from the note: decoy-held-fixed baselines, the isolation/group routing-premium split, a lift that shrinks as the baseline improves, process-versus-outcome lift split, and static scan scores showing no correlation with live lift (rho near 0). The note's sources list does not include 2608.20614.
- The note has no coverage of discovery or routing pressure as the number of available skills grows.
- Second-best fit: the "Routing vs. domain evals in multi-agent systems" subsection (routing premium) or the "Evaluate the components, then the whole" section.
- Another note that could fit: 10-evals-in-ci.md (evaluation-native, change-aware CI with evals/ next to the skill; progressive depth from structural checks to live runs). I did not read it. It is a plausible secondary home. 04-graders.md or 05-llm-as-judge.md fit the 0.14 scan disagreement and the judge spread, but those are weaker.

CODE / SCHEMA worth keeping (verbatim)
- Lift formula (§4.7): "Lift𝑠,𝑎 = 1/|M| ∑_{m∈M} S^with_{s,a,m} − S^base_{s,a,m}"
- Outcome view (App. A): "L_outcome = ½(L_accuracy + L_goal accuracy). For the frozen headline this is (0.1431+ 0.2167)/2 = 0.1799."
- evals.json entry fields (§4.1): unique id, user question, expected_skill (null for negatives), optional expected_script, ground_truth, ordered expected_behavior strings. Example behaviors: "read git-skill/SKILL.md before executing"; "confirmed destructive operation with the user before proceeding".

FIGURE CANDIDATES
- Fig 6 (p9): Isolation versus group testing, with Lift_grp minus Lift_iso = routing premium. It explains the decomposition faster than prose.
- Fig 10 (p12): per-harness baseline vs with-skill bars, plus the Codex model sweep showing lift shrinking as the baseline rises. It is the single best picture of why paired measurement matters.
- Fig 8 (p10): lift by metric with the % positive. It shows process metrics beating outcome metrics.
- Fig 1 (p4): the scatter showing structural vs judge disagreement.
- Fig 3 (p6): pipeline overview.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
- Extraction was clean, with some ligature and spacing glitches (for example "reportsSkill Lift", "DROPTABLE"). Figure values (Fig 8 and 10) come from extracted text labels, not from viewing the images.
- The first Bash call's output was truncated in the tool, so I re-extracted to /tmp/aces.txt (a scratch file, not a deliverable) and read it in full from there.
- The PDF is 15 pages.
